question: Explain why the electrical conductivity of an intrinsic semiconductor is higher than that of an insulator but lower than that of a metal. Give reason using energy band concept.

options.A: Intrinsic semiconductors have greater conductivity than metals because their energy gap is zero.
options.B: Intrinsic semiconductors behave as insulators because their forbidden gap is infinite.
options.C: All three materials have the same energy gap, so their conductivities are equal.
options.D: Metals have overlapping or partially filled bands and many free electrons. Insulators have a large forbidden gap and almost no carriers. Intrinsic semiconductors have a small gap, so some carriers are thermally excited; hence their conductivity lies between metals and insulators.
